[signal_reanalysis] R0's g4 rationale re-interpreted: (a) 0.02 dB PSNR tie on pair0 is < 3 dB and the sim PSNR is dominated by an unrepresentable tone residual (R0 plateau 26.6-27.1 dB across 12 candidates), so it cannot rank blur severity; (b) kernel-shape metrics (pca/density/flatness) are non-discriminative under JPEG - g3 sim (pca 1.090, density 0.719, flatness 0.413) and g4 sim (1.131, 0.765, 0.410) are both classified as glass (known FP; glass_score 1.25 in every sim); (c) block_boundary magnitude is a blur x JPEG interaction signal and its mismatch direction (target blockier than all sims) is inconsistent with dct_zero_ratio (target less zeroed than every sim), i.e. an encoder-level difference, not a blur severity.

[statistical_check] NO_NOISE confirmed on all 5 pairs: (1) noise_prior sigma 0.37-1.61 < 2; (2) known-noise-free g3+j4 simulation yields the IDENTICAL wavelet sigma (1.48 per channel) as the target against the same clean -> zero differential evidence; (3) peeled section-B extreme_pct is degenerate on signed residuals (noise-free target-clean residual = 61.60%, peeled = 75.13%, and a real noise_impulse:1 test gives 99.50%) -> not evidence of impulse; (4) per-channel saturated pixels in targets (==0: 0.0002-0.117%, ==255: 0.0000-0.044%) are far below noise_impulse sev1 (~1% of channel elements) and LOWER than the cleans (pair4 clean 2.58% at 255); any post-blur impulse would leave saturated pixels, and any pre-blur impulse is attenuated by the sigma-3 blur to ~1/255 (unidentifiable). No noise step added.
